title: Trust Workbench — attestation lab notes (Juliette)
content:
Context / goal:
- Quick personal lab notes for the Trust Workbench experiment. Trying to turn the big SOC2 control-mapping task into small runnable checks we can hand to SRE/infra and a junior SME. Not a final artifact — intentionally messy.

High-level framing (one-liner):
- Build a small, repeatable attestation bench that exercises key control families (access, keys, change control, deploys, logging) so we can produce targeted evidence samples for auditors and then generalize into the playbook.

Top hypotheses to validate this week:
1) We can produce a 10-minute evidence package for a single API-key rotation event (key creation -> use -> rotate -> revoke + audit entries).
2) Keystore audit logs contain sufficient fields to map to CC6/CC7 (who, when, action, resource id, outcome).
3) Minimal automation (one script + one manual sign-off) will cut evidence collection time by ~60% for the specific happy-path.

Quick risk/questions (things to answer in pairing sessions):
- Q: Which keystore does Dedicated customers use vs hosted? Different control owners. Need label mapping.
- Q: Are key creation/retrieval events correlated across two logs (keystore + API proxy)? If so, timestamp sync/resolution matters.
- Q: Retention window for keystore debug logs vs audit logs — are we covered for 90-day evidence pulls?
- Q: How do HSM-backed keys appear in logs (masked ids)?

Sketch: control -> minimal evidence mapping (very rough)
- Control: Logical access — API keys + console access
  - Evidence: user account list export (CSV), MFA enforcement screenshot, example API key rotation event (audit lines)
  - Where to get it: IAM admin UI, keystore logs, auth-service /sessions API

- Control: Change management for infra changes
  - Evidence: PR + CI pipeline run ID + deployment trace (git sha -> container image -> node deployment timestamps)
  - Where to get it: GitHub PR link, CI job URL, k8s rollout events

- Control: Logging and monitoring (supply chain for audit events)
  - Evidence: sample log lines (keystore, proxy), retention policy doc, alert rule that would trigger on revoked-key use
  - Where to get it: ELK/CloudWatch query, observability runbook

Evidence collection checklist (for the 10-min demo package):
- [ ] Identify a low-risk test key (dev tenant) and note owner + TTL.
- [ ] Run key create via test harness (script included below) and capture request id + timestamp.
- [ ] Use key to sign a small request (capture API gateway access log entry).
- [ ] Rotate key (call rotate endpoint) — capture rotation event id and resulting metadata.
- [ ] Attempt to use old key and capture the rejected request + alerting (if any).
- [ ] Export Keystore audit lines covering the above timeframe (raw JSON + human-friendly excerpt).
- [ ] Produce short narrative (2–3 bullets) mapping each artifact to the relevant SOC2 control objective.

Quick script prototype (pseudo):
- ./attest-demo.sh --env=dev --op=create --label=trustbench-2026
  - POST /v1/keys -> returns key_id, request_id, user_id
  - GET /v1/keystore/logs?request_id=<id> -> tail matching lines
  - POST /v1/keys/<key_id>/rotate -> returns new_key_id, rotation_request_id
  - curl with old key -> expect 401 (capture gateway log id)

Notes on log gaps / challenges I've hit:
- timestamps between proxy and keystore are off by ~1–2s; correlation needs request_id propagation. If request_id missing we need to fallback to user+ip+ts window which is messy.
- some keystore events are written to different indices depending on whether HSM or softkey was used — search needs OR across indices.
- developer-friendly sample extracts must redact PII and key material; auditors need the mapping but not raw keys.

Manual sign-off pattern (proposed):
- After running the automated steps, a security SME reviews the raw audit extract and adds a short note: "Confirmed: key rotate event lines present, old-key rejection observed". SME signs off in a small markdown note attached to evidence bundle.

Work-items / TODO (next 2 days):
- [ ] Pair with Rhea to find a dev tenant that has keystore debug enabled (R: Rhea) — target: 2026-02-20
- [ ] Prototype the small script to run create/use/rotate/reuse flow (R: me) — target: 2026-02-22
- [ ] Check retention policy for audit index (ask Ian) (R: Ian) — target: 2026-02-21
- [ ] Draft the 2–3 bullet narrative template for auditors (R: me + Ian) — target: 2026-02-23

Handy references / ticket links (todo: move to confluence):
- SEC-4823: keystore audit correlation (jira)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/keystore/compare/attest-demo (WIP)
- Confluence: Trust Workbench — initial design (WIP)

Open ideas (parking lot):
- Can we create an "evidence view" in console that bundles audit lines + short narrative + redaction meta for quick download? Low-hanging UX win.
- Explore using signed short-lived evidence bundles (zip + signature) for auditors to verify provenance.
- Auto-classify events by control family using heuristics (e.g., keywords: rotate, revoke, grant) — would be useful across L1-L3 evidence pulls.

Random scribbles (notes to self):
- If retention < 90d — need a scheduled snapshot job that writes minimal audit buckets to long-term storage.
- Need to avoid copying key material into evidence exports — add filter in script to strip 'key_value' fields by default.
- Consider a 'demo' tenant env var so automation doesn't touch prod scopes.

Meeting prep for pairing session with Ian / Rhea (agenda):
- 5m: goal recap + success criteria for the demo
- 15m: walk through script flow and expected log lines (live run?)
- 10m: identify any permissions/retention blockers
- 10m: assign next actions + deadlines

Final quick callouts:
- This is intentionally slim — the idea is to create one repeatable happy-path first. Once we have a clean example, iterate to cover exception/error flows and multi-tenant mapping.
- Keep evidence bundles short and narrative-led: auditors appreciate a 1-paragraph map + 3 artifacts rather than a raw 10k-line dump.

-- Juliette (scratchpad)
